Kazi Ali Zahir alias Elin  and others  ------ Appellant-Petitioners
Vs

full_judgment:
Afzal Hossain Ahmed J : This appeal is directed against the order dated 6-10-2003 passed by the learned Judge of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal No. 1, Chandpur in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 24 of 2002 rejecting the application for recalling the prosecution witnesses under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 2. 	The case of the prosecution is that, the appellants were being tried for the murder of one Bilkis Akhter @ Bilo, wife of the accused-appellant No. 1, in the aforesaid Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 24 of 2002 under section 4(1)111 (Ka)/30 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. In the meantime as many as 15 PWs have been examined and cross-examined and the accused-appellants and two others were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the accused-appellants pleaded not guilty and prayed for adducing defence witness. That on 21-9-2003 the case was fixed for DWs and on the same day the learned Advocate for the appellants on perusal of the case records found that due to inadvertence and by bona fide mistake some material questions have not been suggested to the prosecution witnesses and, as such, filed an application under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for recalling the prosecution witness Nos. 1, 2, 5 and 6 but the learned Tribunal Judge by its order dated 21-9-2003 rejected the said prayer. Then again, the accused-appellants filed another application specifically mentioning the proposed questions and suggestions what the accused-appellants intended to put to the PWs 1, 2, 5 and 6 and it was contended that these were essential to the just decision of the case and had the accused-appellants not been given that opportunity they would be seriously prejudiced. That the learned Tribunal Judge without considering those essential aspects of the matter rejected the application under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure vide the impugned order dated 6-10-2003 holding an erroneous view that after examination of 15 prosecution witnesses and closure of the prosecution evidence and also after examination of the accused-appellants under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure there was no scope for consideration of the aforesaid petition which is not tenable in law. 

 5. The learned Advocate for the accused- appellants submits that the accused-appellants in the petition under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure had mentioned the proposed questions to be put to the PWs 1,2,5 and 6 for the ends of justice but the court below without considering the judicial aspect of the prayer whether it is essential to the just decision of the case misconceived in holding that there is no scope for consideration of the petition as the prosecution evidence have been closed and the accused have been examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 6. The learned Advocate further submits that proposed questions what the accused-appellants intend to put to the PWs 1, 2, 5 and 6 are essential to the just decision of the case and the same having not been done to fill up the lacuna the rejection of the application without considering that aspect amounts to causing miscarriage of justice to the accused-appellants. 

 7. Mr Md Abdul Alim Mia, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-appellants, in appreciation of his submission, has referred to the decisions in the case of Hemayetuddin @ Auranga vs State reported in 1994 BLD (AD) 9, Mohiuddin Howlader vs State reported in 1994 BLD 82 and Shamsul Haque Ladu and another vs State reported in 2000 BLD 531. 

 8. Section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is expressed in the widest possible tern, and it cannot be said that the intention of this section is to limit its application to the witnesses only before examination of the accused under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The power is available to the court and under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure a court has power to recall any witness and to re-examine him either of its own motion or at the instance of a party at any stage of the inquiry, trial or other proceeding under this Code "if his evidence appears to it essential to the just decision of the case". 

 10. It appears from the impugned order dated 6-10-2003 that the court below while disposing of the said application under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the accused- appellants had erred in law in holding an erroneous view that after examination of 15 PWs and closure of the prosecution evidence and also as because the accused had been examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure there was no scope for consideration of the said application under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure without considering the facts whether the proposed questions and suggestions intended to be put to PWs 1, 2, 5 and 6 by recalling them are essential to the just decision of the case. On consideration of the application under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the accused-appellants in the court below we find that the proposed questions and suggestions intended to be put to the PWs 1, 2, 5 and 6 by recalling them are essential to the just decision of the case and had they not been given such opportunity it may cause miscarriage of justice. 

 11. The learned Deputy Attorney-General opposing the accused-appellants submissions has cited a decision in the case of Nozrul Islam @ Monto vs Stale reported in 1999 BLD 188 but we find that the facts and circumstances of the case under report are distinguishable from that of the instant case. 

 12. Considering all the above aspects of the matter as well as taking into consideration the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the accused-appellants as referred to above, we find merit in this appeal and, as such, we are inclined to hold that the application under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,in question, filed by the accused-appellants in the court below for recalling the PWs should be allowed to meet the ends of justice and such scope is available inasmuch as the trial of the case is not yet concluded. 

 13. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed and the impugned order dated 6-10-2003 passed by the learned Judge of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal No.1, Chandpur in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No. 24 of 2002 rejecting the application filed by the accused-appellants for re-calling the prosecution witnesses under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is hereby set aside. 

 The application, in question, for recalling the prosecution witnesses under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is allowed. With a view to eliciting contradiction from the statements of PWs 5 and 6 recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as disclosed in the aforesaid application under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure attention of the Investigating Officer may be required to be drawn and  as such  he should also be recalled. The learned Tribunal Judge is directed to proceed with the case in the light of the observations made above and according to law.
